asset.name: UndoableDestructiveAction
asset.description: The destructive-action pattern preferring reversible removal with visible undo, escalating to explicit confirmation only where reversal is genuinely impossible, and handling undo that itself fails.

requires.reason: The reversal affordance and its expiry are shared.
Reversal, grouping, and expiry belong to the shared history service.
User-facing copy resolves through the adopting host locale bridge.

suggests.reason: Only genuinely irreversible actions should escalate to a modal confirmation.

signatureMoment.description: A destructive action completes immediately and offers a visible, time-bounded way back, so the product feels forgiving instead of interrogative.

rationale: Inverts the usual reflex. Confirmation dialogs train users to click through them; reversible deletion with visible undo is both safer and faster, and confirmation should be reserved for the rare truly irreversible case.
